title: The Silicon Psyche: Anthropomorphic Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Adversarial prompt scenarios simulating authority figures (e.g., CISO impersonation) in SOC environments to test unquestioning compliance and security reporting inhibition, scored on a Green/Yellow/Red ternary scale.
Using prompt scenarios that manufacture artificial urgency or time pressure (e.g., failing databases) to evaluate if the LLM bypasses standard security controls.
Evaluating LLM decision-making against Cialdini's influence principles using prompts that present false social proof, scarcity, or reciprocity exploitation.
Testing LLM deference to claimed 'automated system' outputs and willingness to accept AI hallucinations when processing information from other synthetic agents.
Injecting fear-based, anger-induced, or stress-associated linguistic patterns into prompts to observe if the model simulates corresponding affective responses or tunnel vision.
Measuring performance degradation, information overload paralysis, and complexity-induced errors in scenarios exceeding model-specific context windows.
